outputs.L1: Improvements and modifications to coil steel straighteners include an integrated structural head that enables faster equipment setup; lower backup rolls integrated into the structural head; self-aligning rollers; setup timing blocks for equipment calibration; and adjustment screw jacks that permit narrower center distances and incorporate internal pointers and scales. The backup rollers for each work roller are supported on separate backup roller plates, allowing them to be removably installed and independently adjusted. The backup rollers may be supported between opposing blocks and adjusted by moving the blocks toward or away from the backup roller plate using leveling jacks. The work rollers associated with the upper bank may be supported between opposing slide blocks that move vertically within slots formed in opposing side plates, with visual indicators establishing a zero position for each work roller in the upper bank.
outputs.L2:
An upgraded coil-steel straightener uses a unified structural head designed to reduce equipment setup time. The head incorporates the lower backup rolls, self-centering rollers, calibration timing blocks, and adjusting screw jacks. These jacks permit tighter center spacing and contain internal pointers and measurement scales.

Each work roll has backup rollers mounted on its own dedicated plate, allowing them to be removed and adjusted separately from those serving other work rolls. The backup rollers can be positioned between two opposing blocks, with leveling jacks shifting the blocks toward or away from the backup-roller plate. For the upper roll bank, the work rolls may be held between facing slide blocks that travel vertically within slots in opposite side plates. Visual indicators identify the zero setting for each upper-bank work roll.
outputs.L3:
The integrated structural head is designed to streamline equipment setup while incorporating lower backup rolls for added support. Self-aligning rollers, calibration timing blocks, and adjustment screw jacks further improve alignment accuracy and simplify setup procedures.

The screw jacks support narrower center distances and feature internal pointers and scales for precise, repeatable adjustments. Separate backup roller plates allow the backup rollers for each work roller to be removed and adjusted independently, improving maintenance access and setup flexibility.

In the upper bank, the work rollers move vertically within slide-block slots. Visual indicators make it easy to establish a consistent zero position, supporting accurate calibration and reliable operation.
outputs.L4:
The improved coil steel straightener incorporates a rigid, integrated structural head that supports the principal straightening components within a unified assembly. This construction increases structural stability, reduces unwanted deflection, and simplifies machine setup and maintenance. Lower backup rolls reinforce the work rollers during operation, helping the machine withstand the substantial forces generated as coiled steel is flattened and straightened.

Self-aligning rollers compensate for minor installation or operating misalignments and promote more uniform contact across the width of the steel strip. Calibration blocks provide reliable reference points for establishing roller positions, allowing operators to verify machine settings quickly and repeatably. Compact screw jacks, equipped with internal scales, permit precise positional adjustments while requiring less installation space than conventional adjustment mechanisms. The internal scales also protect the measurement system and enable operators to reproduce previously established settings.

The backup-roll and work-roller assemblies can be adjusted independently. As a result, each assembly may be aligned and calibrated without disturbing the position of the other. This independent control enables operators to compensate for variations in strip thickness, width, material strength, and incoming coil curvature. It also allows the backup rolls to provide appropriate support while the work rollers are positioned to achieve the desired straightening effect.

The compact arrangement permits narrower spacing between adjacent rollers, improving control over the steel as it passes through the machine. Reduced roller spacing can produce more consistent bending and reverse-bending action, thereby improving flatness and straightening accuracy. Together, the integrated head, supported roller arrangement, self-aligning components, calibration features, and precise adjustment mechanisms reduce setup time, simplify calibration, and improve repeatability. The resulting straightener offers greater operational efficiency, more accurate alignment, and improved finished-strip quality.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical abstract explaining the structural head, backup roller adjustment, leveling jacks, and upper work roller positioning in an improved coil straightening machine.
counterfactuals.output: An improved coil straightening machine employs a rigid structural head that supports and maintains alignment of the roll assemblies under high separating loads. Adjustable backup rollers reinforce the work rollers and permit compensation for roll deflection, material thickness, and desired flatness. Leveling jacks provide precise vertical alignment of the head and roll frame, ensuring a uniform pass line across the machine width. The upper work rollers are independently or collectively positionable relative to the lower rollers to establish roll gap, penetration, and bending pattern. Together, these features improve setup accuracy, load distribution, strip flatness, and repeatability while reducing frame distortion and maintenance requirements.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: What modifications does the invention make to conventional coil steel straighteners, and how do they improve setup, calibration, and independent roller adjustment?
counterfactuals.output:
The invention retrofits a conventional coil-steel straightener by:

- **Separating the normally ganged upper-roll assembly** so each work roller can move vertically on its own.
- **Providing each roller with an individual adjustment mechanism**—typically a screw/jack or actuator—with a calibrated position indicator and lock.
- **Adding a common calibration or “zero” reference**, established with a straight calibration plate, bar, or gauge between the upper and lower rolls.

These changes improve operation in three ways:

1. **Faster setup:** Operators can set roll penetration directly from known readings or saved settings instead of repeatedly feeding and checking strip.
2. **Repeatable calibration:** All roll positions are referenced to the same pass line, compensating for assembly tolerances, roll wear, and maintenance changes.
3. **Independent adjustment:** Each roller can be raised or lowered without moving the others, allowing the operator to create the desired progressively decreasing bend pattern and correct localized flatness or shape problems without disturbing the entire setup.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert the patent claims for an enhanced coil steel straightener into a single clear paragraph, retaining details about removable backup roller plates, opposing blocks, slide blocks, and visual zero-position indicators.
counterfactuals.output: An enhanced coil steel straightener comprises a frame supporting multiple straightening rollers, removable backup roller plates positioned to support the straightening rollers and permit convenient removal, replacement, or maintenance, opposing blocks arranged on opposite sides of the straightening assembly, and slide blocks movably received by the opposing blocks to adjust the position and pressure of the rollers. The straightener further includes visual zero-position indicators associated with the adjustable components, enabling an operator to identify a reference position, accurately set the roller spacing or pressure, and repeat prior settings.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an improved roller straightener design that integrates lower backup rolls, self-aligning rollers, setup timing blocks, narrow-center screw jacks, and independently adjustable backup rollers.
counterfactuals.output:
### Improved Roller Straightener Design

The straightener uses alternating upper and lower work rolls to remove coil set, crossbow, and localized strip distortion. Its frame incorporates the following improvements:

- **Lower backup-roll assemblies:** Each highly loaded lower work roll is supported by one or more backup rolls mounted beneath it. These reduce work-roll deflection, increase straightening force capacity, and improve flatness across the strip width.

- **Self-aligning rollers:** Backup rolls and critical support rollers are mounted in spherical bearings or pivoting cartridges. They automatically conform to minor shaft, frame, and roll misalignment, distributing load evenly and minimizing edge loading, wear, and marking.

- **Setup timing blocks:** Removable or adjustable timing blocks mechanically establish the relative starting positions of the roll stations. During setup or maintenance, the blocks synchronize the upper and lower roll elevations, provide repeatable pass-line and penetration settings, and reduce dependence on manual measurement.

- **Narrow-center screw jacks:** Compact screw jacks are positioned on close centers along the machine width or length. Their slim housings fit between adjacent roll stations while providing precise vertical adjustment and high load capacity. The jacks may be mechanically linked for normal synchronized movement and selectively disengaged for calibration.

- **Independently adjustable backup rollers:** Each lower backup roller is carried in its own vertically adjustable cassette, actuated by a dedicated screw, wedge, hydraulic cylinder, or servo jack. Operators can vary support at individual locations to compensate for work-roll crown, wear, thermal distortion, or asymmetric strip loading. Position indicators or closed-loop sensors permit settings to be stored and repeated.

A rigid, windowed frame provides access for cartridge removal, timing-block installation, and roll servicing. In operation, the timing blocks establish the baseline geometry, the narrow-center jacks set overall roll penetration, and the independent backup adjustments fine-tune the loaded roll profile. The self-aligning mounts then accommodate residual angular error while maintaining uniform contact.

The combined design delivers higher straightening force, reduced lower-roll bending, faster and more repeatable setup, improved strip flatness, longer roll and bearing life, and easier maintenance.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
